meta.task: US 2017 energy indicators (solar potential / renewable deployment / electricity price / carbon intensity) -> correlation assessment -> federal incentive priority; deliver a 2x3 multi-source figure 'output.png'
meta.env_note: pandas 3.1.1 / numpy 2.5.4 / matplotlib 3.11.2 available; run_python uses -I so `sys.path.append('/Users/mac/Library/Python/3.13/lib/python/site-packages')` is required before imports. Use matplotlib 'Agg' backend explicitly.

objective.policy_question: Which states should receive priority federal solar incentives in 2017, given the interplay of solar resource, existing renewable deployment, retail electricity price and fossil (carbon-intensive) generation mix?
analysis_questions: Q1: How do the five state-level indicators co-vary (correlation structure), and which axes summarize them (PCA)?
Q2: Is solar resource aligned with high electricity prices (the classic incentive-justification argument)? (verified: NO, r=-0.09)
Q3: Are the sunniest states also the most fossil-dependent (abatement leverage)? (verified: r=+0.30)
Q4: What is the unit-consistent, rank-robust way to score states for incentive priority?
objective.answer_strategy: Two-track: (a) national/global context panels (world CO2 vs renewables, steel-plant load profiles) illustrate the multi-dimensional framing; (b) the state-level evidence (PCA + correlation + top-10 fossil) drives the priority ranking. The ranking must be reported with its four underlying indicators, not as a black-box score.

derived/state_2017_features.csv.grain: one row per state + DC, calendar 2017
derived/state_2017_features.csv.note: 175 nulls exist only in raw per-source generation columns (e.g. Geothermal 44, Pumped Storage 33, Other Gases 29) where the state has no such source; treat as 0 for any stacked/summed use, never for shares (shares already computed upstream).

Google Project Sunroof/*.note: Each file contains 1-2 rows with NaN region_name -> dropna(subset=['region_name']) before summing; totals agree within ~1.6% so aggregation is effectively additive across granularities.

Steel_industry_data.csv.note: date must be parsed day-first: pd.to_datetime(..., format='%d/%m/%Y %H:%M').

U.S._Electricity_Prices.csv.verified: 62 = 51 states+DC + 10 census divisions (New England, Middle Atlantic, East North Central, West North Central, South Atlantic, East South Central, West South Central, Mountain, Pacific Contiguous, Pacific Noncontiguous) + 'U.S. Total'; 744 monthly 2017 residential observations = 62 labels x 12 months
U.S._Electricity_Prices.csv.rule: MUST whitelist the 51 real state names before any state-level aggregation, otherwise 11 aggregate rows silently inflate results. res_price = mean of 12 monthly values of sectorName=='residential', year==2017 (cents/kWh).

US_Energy_Generation_2001-2022.csv.grain: monthly x state x producer type x energy source
US_Energy_Generation_2001-2022.csv.verified: TYPE OF PRODUCER has 6 values -> keep only 'Total Electric Power Industry'; 14 ENERGY SOURCE values incl. 'Total'; STATE includes 'US-TOTAL' which must be dropped (2017 total fossil 2.536e9 MWh national)
US_Energy_Generation_2001-2022.csv.rule: fossil = Coal+Petroleum+Natural Gas+Other Gases summed over MONTH for YEAR==2017; do not add CHP sub-producers (double counting).

global-data-on-sustainable-energy.csv +.verified_join: Year 2019 inner join on Entity==country with iso_code.notna() and all three of (renewable share, co2_per_capita, population) non-null -> exactly 172 countries; renewable share 0.0-95.03 %, co2_per_capita 0.056-36.25 t
global-data-on-sustainable-energy.csv +.note: Only 1 country (Qatar) exceeds the required ylim upper bound of 30 -> it will be clipped by ylim, which is acceptable per spec; mention clipping in the caption/answer.

pipeline_steps.name: load_state_table
pipeline_steps.action: pd.read_csv('derived/state_2017_features.csv'); assert len==51 and no nulls in model columns

pipeline_steps.name: correlation_matrix
pipeline_steps.action: Pearson r on ['log_kw_total','yearly_sunlight_kwh_median','renew_share','res_price','fossil_share','deploy_per_1k','percent_qualified']; store full matrix + the 7 headline pairs

pipeline_steps.name: pca
pipeline_steps.action: z-score (ddof=0) the 5 features ['log_kw_total','yearly_sunlight_kwh_median','renew_share','res_price','fossil_share']; SVD; keep PC1/PC2 scores; fix eigenvector sign so PC1.renew_share>0 and PC2.res_price<0 (reproduce upstream orientation)

pipeline_steps.name: steel_data
pipeline_steps.action: Load_Type counts for pie; first 672 rows (7 days) sorted by parsed date for the sampled time series

pipeline_steps.name: granularity_totals
pipeline_steps.action: sum kw_total per Project Sunroof granularity after dropna(region_name)

pipeline_steps.name: top10_fossil
pipeline_steps.action: 2017 fossil MWh by state, drop US-TOTAL, sort desc, take 10

pipeline_steps.name: priority_score
pipeline_steps.action: composite z-score ranking, 2 variants + robustness intersection

pipeline_steps.name: render_figure
pipeline_steps.action: 2x3 gridspec, fixed panel order 1-6, suptitle, save 'output.png' dpi=150, bbox/layout as specified

pipeline_steps.name: validate_output
pipeline_steps.action: assert output.png exists and >200 KB; assert all 6 axes titles/labels equal the required strings; assert axes count == 6

panel_specs.name: pca_scatter
panel_specs.title: U.S. States: PCA Analysis of Energy Indicators (colored by electricity price)
panel_specs.data: derived/state_2017_features.csv (51 rows) -> PC1/PC2 scores from z-scored 5 features
panel_specs.plot: ax.scatter(PC1, PC2, c=res_price, cmap='RdYlBu_r', s=80, edgecolor='k', linewidth=0.5, alpha=0.85)
extras: annotate 4-6 extreme states: e.g. HI (max price), NM/AZ (max sunlight), TX (max capacity), VT/ME (right end of PC1)
add axhline/axvline at 0 in light grey
note in-axes text: PC1 40.8% / PC2 23.0% variance (cum. 63.8%)
panel_specs.expected_axis_reading: PC1(+) = clean/renewable & fossil-light (VT, ME, SD, DC); PC1(-) = fossil-heavy + large installed capacity (FL, LA, TX, AZ, NM). PC2 is dominated by cheap electricity (res_price loading -0.69) and capacity (+0.46).

panel_specs.name: global_bubble
panel_specs.title: Global: CO2 Per Capita vs Renewable Energy Share (bubble=population)
panel_specs.data: global-data-on-sustainable-energy.csv (2019 renewable share) INNER JOIN owid-co2-data.csv (2019 co2_per_capita, population) on country name, iso_code notna -> 172 points
panel_specs.plot: ax.scatter(ren_share, co2_per_capita, s=population/1.5e6 + 20, alpha=0.5, edgecolor='k', linewidth=0.4, color='#2c7fb8'); ax.set_xlim(0,100); ax.set_ylim(0,30)
extras: annotate 5 largest bubbles (China, India, United States, Indonesia, Russia) if x<100 and y<30
panel_specs.expected: Negative but loose relationship; the mass sits below 20 t at 10-60% renewable share; a handful of high-co2/low-renewable Gulf states at bottom-right of the clip.

panel_specs.name: steel_load_pie
panel_specs.title: Steel Industry: Load Type Distribution (2018)
panel_specs.data: Steel_industry_data.csv, value_counts of Load_Type over all 35040 intervals
extras: put counts in the legend or labels
panel_specs.why_in_figure: Illustrates that >half of plant operating time is light-load -> efficiency measures at light load matter as much as peak-shaving; supports the 'demand-side' leg of the multi-dimensional framing.

panel_specs.name: granularity_bar
panel_specs.title: Solar Potential Comparison by Geographic Granularity
panel_specs.xlabel: Geographic Granularity (State, County, City, Postal Code)

extras: annotate each bar with value in millions of kW (e.g. '832.5M')

panel_specs.name: top10_fossil_hbar
panel_specs.title: Top 10 U.S. States: Fossil Fuel Generation (2017)
panel_specs.data: US_Energy_Generation_2001-2022.csv: YEAR==2017, TYPE OF PRODUCER=='Total Electric Power Industry', ENERGY SOURCE in [Coal, Petroleum, Natural Gas, Other Gases], sum over MONTH, drop STATE=='US-TOTAL', top 10
panel_specs.plot: ax.barh(states[::-1], values[::-1], color='#b30000' with alpha ramp) so the largest bar is on top
extras: note: 11th is Illinois 73.2M (nearly tied with NC) -> mention tie sensitivity
panel_specs.policy_link: These are the highest absolute abatement pools; crossing with fossil_share identifies states where solar substitution actually displaces carbon (TX, FL, PA, OH, IN overlap with the priority list only when combined with high solar resource).

panel_specs.name: steel_timeseries
panel_specs.title: Steel Industry: Energy Usage Patterns (sampled)
panel_specs.data: Steel_industry_data.csv, parse date day-first, sort, take first 672 rows = 2018-01-01 00:00 .. 2018-01-07 23:45 (7 days at 15-min)
extras: mark weekends (indices 288-479 = Sat+Sun) with axvspan in light grey
caption in answer: mean 27.15 kWh, max 147.5 kWh, visible weekday/weekend cycle
panel_specs.note: 672 points is chosen over the 35040-point full series for legibility in a small panel; alternative df.iloc[::24] (1460 pts) is noisier.

figure_spec.grid: 2 rows x 3 cols (fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(20, 11)))
figure_spec.mandatory_report: The final answer must state that the visualization file is named 'output.png'.

correlation_analysis_plan.method: Pearson r on 51 states, 2017; report absolute MWh alongside share-based metrics

renew_share~fossil_share.reading: partly mechanical (same 'Total' denominator) -> treat as one 'clean vs fossil mix' axis, do not over-interpret

res_price~deploy_per_1k.reading: adoption is economics-driven: expensive states install more -> price is the effective incentive signal

yearly_sunlight_kwh_median~percent_quali.reading: sunnier states have a larger roof-qualified stock

yearly_sunlight_kwh_median~deploy_per_1k.reading: resource drives deployment but only moderately

yearly_sunlight_kwh_median~res_price.reading: KEY NEGATIVE FINDING: resource and price are decoupled -> a price-only federal signal misses the sunniest states

fossil_share~yearly_sunlight_kwh_median.reading: sunniest states are also fossil-heavy -> highest abatement leverage

log_kw_total~renew_share.reading: absolute installable capacity is concentrated in large fossil-heavy states

kw_median~yearly_sunlight_kwh_median.reading: median system size is a good potential-intensity proxy

interpretation_rules: prefer rank-robust checks (Spearman) for small n=51 if a pair is borderline

priority_framework.rationale: Federal dollars should go where (i) the physical resource is high, (ii) the displaced generation is carbon intensive, and (iii) current deployment is low relative to the qualified roof stock. Price enters as a STRESS TEST, not as a core driver, because resource and price are decoupled (r=-0.09).

tier_assignment.Tier 1 (robust, both variants): New Mexico, Mississippi, Florida, Delaware, Arizona, and (borderline) Louisiana/Wyoming/Missouri/Arkansas/Indiana
tier_assignment.Tier 2 (price-driven entries): Rhode Island, Hawaii - enter only via the price term while irradiance is low; support should be efficiency/equity-targeted rather than utility-scale solar
tier_assignment.Tier 3 (low priority): VT, DC, WA, ME, OR - already clean and/or low irradiance

sensitivity_tests_required: weight the resource term x2 (does NM/FL/AZ stay?), drop the price term (variant B), Spearman instead of Pearson for the ranking inputs
report the 4 raw indicators per state next to the score (sunlight, fossil_share, renew_share, deploy_per_1k)
caveats: weights are judgement calls -> report the score AND its components
carbon intensity is proxied by fossil generation share; no state-level emissions data exists in the workspace (owid-co2 has no per-state rows)
Project Sunroof kW totals are modelled installable capacity on qualified roofs, not realised generation

global_2019.note: bubble panel is context only - it must not be used to rank US states

steel_2018.note: single-plant illustrative data - explicitly will not enter the state priority score

validation_checks: len(states)==51 and model columns have zero nulls
PCA explained variance equals [40.84, 23.01, 17.11] (+-0.1) and positive loadings on renew_share in PC1
global join yields exactly 172 rows; xlim [0,100] and ylim [0,30] set exactly
top10 fossil starts with Texas 341.8M MWh and contains no 'US-TOTAL'
output.png exists, 6 axes, suptitle and all 12 required axis titles/labels match the required strings verbatim
risks: share-vs-share correlations are mechanically inflated by a common denominator
no direct state carbon-intensity variable -> fossil_share proxy, disclosed
census-division rows in U.S._Electricity_Prices.csv would corrupt state means if not whitelisted
steel panel is 2018 single-plant data, and the 672-point sample is a deliberate readability choice
one country (Qatar) is clipped by the required ylim [0,30]; mention it rather than changing the limits
priority ranking is weight-sensitive (variant A vs B differ by 3 states: RI, HI, LA/AR); never present a single ordering without the sensitivity note
